text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Bank insurer ING plans to attract customers in 50-plus age group with package combining senior care services with financial services. (p1)
- Dutch Gasunie reaches agreement with Germany's Ruhrgas on the delivery of 90 bn cubic metres of natural gas. (p1)
- Philips Electronics reduces stake in ASM Lithography to 23.9 pct from 35.4 pct. (p1)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM plans to extend the life of its aircraft. (p1)
- Germany's Grundig considers legal action to recover DM 750 million it claims is owned by major shareholder Philips. (p3)
- Rabobank forecasts European beer market will shrink by five percent in next three years. (p3)
- Wafer stepper producer ASM Lithography books more than 60 pct higher 1996 net to Dfl 218 million; company uncertain about further profit growth. (p5)
- Insurers, banks and pension funds buy a stake in Triodos bank, which invests in ethnical and sustainable projects. (p15)
VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch banks want to exchange current pay system for staff into merit pay. (p1)
- Growing number of prominent politicians choose family above a high political office. (p1)
- Staff of Belgium's steel concern Boel puts Hoogovens on the spot by rejecting agreement between unions and management on shedding 800 jobs. (p2)
- Human rights movements think Royal Dutch/Shell still has more to put right on human rights. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Figures of central statistics bureau CBS show powerful job growth in 1996. (p1)
- Dutch house prices rose 9.5 pct last year. (p7)
- Dutch budgetary deficit in 1996 halved from four to 2.1 pct. (p7)
- Food and detergent giant Unilever in conflict with Italian authorities over distribution of ice-cream.
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Road blocks and long waiting hours cost Dutch transporters Dfl 128 million last year, says branch organisation TLN. (p13)
TROUW
- Regional bus companies seek to break power of parent company VSN. (p1)
